## Results

GPA averaged M = 2.36 (SD = 0.50, n = 199) and sleep M = 6.33 (SD = 1.11). Of the students, 55.0% were female (Table 1).
Sleep correlated with GPA, r(197) = .31, p < .001, 95% CI [.18, .43]. The model explained R² = .13 of the variance, F(2, 196) = 15.15, p < .001. Sleep predicted GPA, B = 0.13, SE = 0.03, β = .29, t(186) = 4.40, p < .001, and stress predicted lower GPA, B = -0.12, β = -.19, t(196) = -2.90, p = .004. Gender differences were not significant, t(190.16) = -1.01, p = .314, d = -0.14. The scale was reliable (α = .87). Faculty also mattered, F(2, 196) = 4.21, p = .016.
